HubSpot Company Record (10544) — LaunchPad Metrics (launchpadmetrics.com)

Overview / firmographics
- High-growth SaaS account; originally self-serve (Hosted API) and ramped quickly post-feature launch.
- Primary usage: customer chat summarization + internal doc search for support agents.
- Current deployment: Hosted API only (public cloud). No VPC requirement at this time.

What they’re building / workload notes
- Workloads:
  - Summarization (longer outputs; bursty at top-of-hour job runs)
  - Support-agent assist (interactive; latency-sensitive)
  - Doc-search (embeddings + reranking; steady background load)
- Reported pain:
  - Frequent 429s during burst windows; some user-visible failures due to aggressive client retries.
  - Intermittent timeouts when multiple concurrent requests pile up (likely retry storms + queued latency).
- Latency target (stated on call): “<2s time-to-first-token for agent workflows; summaries can be slower but must complete reliably.”

Current state / issues observed
- Support ticket SUP-4922 (self-serve): "frequent 429s after launch"; confusion about rate limits + how retries should behave.
- Pattern: traffic spikes trigger 429s, client retries immediately (no jitter), causing follow-on congestion. They also had a few timeout complaints that appear correlated with the same spike windows.
- They were previously using a single project for both batch summarization + interactive agent traffic (no separation by workload).

Recommendations provided (validated / safe-to-share)
- Client retry guidance (per Support playbook / known-issues drafts):
  - Implement exponential backoff with jitter on HTTP 429 and transient 5xx.
  - Respect Retry-After (when present) and cap max retry attempts.
  - Avoid synchronized retries across workers (randomized jitter).
  - Use shorter connect timeouts + longer overall request timeouts for batch summaries; keep interactive paths strict.
  - Separate batch jobs from interactive agent traffic into different queues/processes to prevent self-induced contention.
- Quota/rate-limit hygiene:
  - Confirm org vs project limits; verify which API keys map to which project.
  - Split workloads into separate projects so batch summarization can’t starve agent assist.
  - Request burst limit increase only after retry behavior is corrected (otherwise it masks the issue).
- Upgrade path discussed:
  - Dedicated as next step if they need predictable throughput for campaign weeks + stronger isolation.
  - Positioning: Dedicated pool + tuned autoscaling/burst to handle peak load; hosted remains fine for baseline.

Quota changes / actions taken
- 2026-02-18: Support helped them identify misread project limits (they were looking at org-level documentation but using a restricted project key).
- 2026-02-19: Temporary quota bump approved to unblock launch week while they ship client retry changes (not a permanent fix).
- 2026-02-22: Follow-up note: they plan to roll out backoff+jitter changes in their Python service this week; asked for “recommended defaults we can point engineering to.”
  - Pointed to internal references: SDK guidance work in progress (redwood-sdk-python PR_519) + known issue draft (429 throttling / quota misconfiguration).

Activity timeline (recent)
- 2026-02-14: Spike in 429 volume reported in-app; Support engaged; initial triage + request for request-ids.
- 2026-02-15: SUP-4922 created; determined issue was rate-limit + retry behavior; provided standard backoff guidance.
- 2026-02-19: Quota temporarily adjusted; advised splitting batch vs interactive traffic.
- 2026-02-22: CS check-in (Rachel Kim) re: upgrade options; customer asked about Dedicated pricing + lead time.

Stakeholders / contacts (internal)
- Owner: Jordan Blake
- SE assist: Alex Martinez (DevEx sponsor asked to provide SDK retry standards pointers)
- CS: Rachel Kim

Open questions
- Need their traffic profile:
  - Baseline QPS vs peak QPS
  - Typical prompt+completion tokens by endpoint
  - Concurrency settings + worker count
- Timeouts: confirm whether they’re client-side timeouts vs server timeouts; request sample request-ids and timestamps.

Next steps
- Book 30-min scoping call: Dedicated sizing + confirm required SLO (peak throughput + acceptable p95 latency).
- Ask customer to share:
  - retry policy config (max retries, base delay, max delay)
  - timeout settings
  - representative request-ids from a 429 window
- If upgrade pursued: prep Dedicated proposal with burst capacity option; otherwise keep on Hosted with corrected retries + project separation.

Linked artifacts
- Jira: SUP-4922
- Drive: top-escalations-analysis-feb-2026.json (contains 429s/timeouts as top drivers)
- Engineering reference: redwood-sdk-python PR_519 (improved retry/backoff + error messaging) / known-issues page draft for 429 troubleshooting
